hypothesis: On the banked register file, the operand fetch waits for the instruction's whole stall decision (stall_other: every scoreboard lookup, every busy unit, the writeback reservation) before asking the banks, which puts that decision in series with the bank arbiters: 6.2 ns post-synthesis and 77 % routing, the kind of path that grows most in place and route. Only a vector source whose producer is still in flight can make a fetched value stale -- only an older instruction can write the register, and every older writer is in the scoreboard -- so gating the fetch on the vector-source hazards alone is safe, takes the stall decision off the path, and lets the fetch overlap the other stalls.
evidence_for_hypothesis: tnca_fpga_top post-synthesis, 6.667 ns target, after timing-008: r_major -> g_vrf_banked.u_vrf/g_bank[2].u_bank/s1_byp_mask 6.166 ns / 25 levels, route 76.6 %: R-stage decode -> stall_other (12 levels) -> of_want -> bank arbitration. The routed worst path of the 75 MHz image (x_pm_idx -> w_vdata) was 80 % routing at 1.6x its post-synthesis delay.
